correctness.rationale: The centered polar norm is exactly the reciprocal inradius by intrinsic polarity and central symmetry. Exhaustive spanning tight-edge graph classification reduces core potentials to two sign families and a tight leaf edge. Returning-leaf type II has norm at most p, strictly below p+4-epsilon_p/N; minimization of integer sign imbalance gives the two exact maxima and unique crossover q=p+3. Sign-binomial counts give all maximal facets, and linear equations on their normals plus finite strict slack for other facets give the full incenter affine ranks. The submitted verifier was executed after construction: independent exact integer enumeration 6 cases/184 polar vertices, 28 profiles/66224 polar vertices and 17116 contact normals, and 9044 arithmetic comparisons; all passed. Finite checks supplement rather than replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The family is a natural single-leaf modification of a complete-bipartite graph, retaining nontrivial cycles and a two-parameter unbounded geometry. The exact inradius, contact multiplicities and center-set dimension exhibit a sharp combinatorial threshold at q=p+3 with a parity-sensitive unique-vs-segment incenter distinction at equality. The strict screened-returning-leaf lemma and contact-normal rank mechanism supply transferable structural insight beyond a finite census.
